prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right one depends on your priorities (lowest premium, deductible vs. copays, access to certain doctors, need for help with ACA subsidies, willingness to pay a broker fee, etc.). I can help you find the best fit, but first a few quick, practical pointers and options.

What to use
- Local independent health insurance broker or agent (best if you want someone who will shop multiple carriers and explain local provider networks).
- A certified Marketplace assister/Navigator if you need help with ACA enrollments and subsidies on healthcare.gov.
- Large online brokers (eHealth, GoHealth) if you want quick quotes and plan comparisons online.

Why choose an independent/local broker
- They can compare plans across multiple carriers (Blue KC, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Cigna, Ambetter, etc.).
- They often know local provider networks and can confirm if your doctor is in‑network.
- They can help with marketplace subsidy eligibility, Special Enrollment Periods, and year‑to‑year renewals.

How to find a good broker in Kansas City, MO
- Look for “independent” or “local” agent (not captive to one carrier).
- Confirm they’re licensed in Missouri and have good reviews (Google/Yelp).
- Check credentials: NAHU membership or Missouri Department of Insurance agent lookup.
- Ask whether they’re certified to assist with the federal Marketplace (healthcare.gov) if you need subsidies.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- Do you work with multiple carriers? Which ones?
- Do you charge a fee (beyond commissions)? If so, how much and when?
- Are you certified to enroll people on healthcare.gov?
- How will you help me at renewal time or if I need to file a claim?
- Can you show me side‑by‑side cost comparisons for plans (premiums, deductibles, OOP max, network)?
- Do you have references from other self‑employed clients?

Resources you can use now
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance: agent lookup and complaint history.
- NAHU “Find an Agent” directory.
- healthcare.gov Assister Locator (for Marketplace help).
- Online brokers: eHealth, GoHealth (for quick comparisons).

If you want, I can:
- Find and list top‑rated independent brokers or agencies near your ZIP code in Kansas City, MO.
- Compare 2–3 plan options (you’d need to tell me age(s), ZIP code, tobacco status, and whether it’s individual or family coverage).

Tell me which you prefer (get names of local brokers vs. online options, or have me pull specific local recommendations) and your ZIP code and plan type, and I’ll pull together a short list of highly rated brokers and what they specialize in.
